design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (payoff_heir_and_borrower_payoffs, env_0064), REWORK round 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,5,5,6]; assigned daily accrual 5, statement 6, approval 6, remittance 5.

WHY THIS TEST. Lorraine Whitcombe's HECM matured (Principal Residence Change, called due 2025-12-21, extended once, referred to foreclosure 2026-09-20). She asks to pay it off today and keep her condominium; the scored root is her own wire amount (owner=user). The agent must discover a 3-hop chain she never mentions (daily accrual -> statement -> HUD due-and-payable approval -> remittance), each hop a multi-factor computation over the HECM ledger, the Fully Funded LESA and its bills, the occupancy profile's inspections and the maturity case, then hand the remittance to her. One tool per problem; no near-synonym tools.

SCOPE. Claimed (task 0): payoff_ext_retention_daily_accrual / record_payoff_daily_accrual_16b003bd; payoff_ext_retention_statement_balance / issue_retention_payoff_statement_a856e53a; payoff_ext_retention_payoff_approval / approve_appraisal_based_payoff_a02ac9a5; payoff_ext_retention_remittance / remit_borrower_payoff_funds_17f1493b (owner=user). Scope of all four: a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due_and_payable, extension_period or foreclosure_referred. Left for task 1: the Approved Short Sale Payoff chain of a living borrower. Compute constraint: CUST is the payoff requester, so cross-category reads only reach a living borrower's own records; both tasks therefore use a living borrower.

HUD REALISM (SF-1). The approval is HUD's due-and-payable payoff: the lesser of the amount owed (statement plus recoverable resolution charges less a company credit) and 95 percent of the maturity case's current appraisal (24 CFR 206.125(c)); no appraisal substitution (SP-1 closed: the base appraisal sentence is not retired and is followed). In this world the borrower has equity (cap 608000.00 > balance figure 424310.66), so she pays the balance figure, as HUD requires.

BVP acceptance_required false, so funds need no signature.

PERSONA. Polite, anxious retired librarian; volunteers name, the foreclosure letter, the goal (pay off today, keep the condo, be told the amount, wire from own savings in own name). Phone and SSN only on request; occupancy, Dana's wires and her own checks only when asked; generic consent when told something must be prepared; one re-check request if the figure seems large; sends the wire on hand-over; ends when told the money is received. No prerequisite named (closes the round-1 SOURCE-CHAIN pattern).

PROBLEM TREE CARD. root payoff_ext_retention_remittance; edges R->P (required_on_case), P->A (stmt_on_case), A->X (per_diem_on_case), all value_input, state form (sentences in prerequisite_closure). Opening evidence: per_diem 0.00, status opened, statement 0.00, appraisal basis and required 0.00. Deletion sensitivity: skip X -> statement 420156.58; skip A -> approval 1765.40; skip P -> remittance 242467.81; root on the opening world 246.00. Each state is brought about by exactly one write of this difficulty within the retention scope (the short-sale tools write the same fields only on Approved Short Sale cases).

PROBES (decoy / absent / edge, rule-equal outcomes): second received tax bill with an earlier due date -> the latest-due bill is counted, per diem unchanged 85.31; no inspection result -> preservation carry 0.00, per diem 85.23; no nonoccupancy_date -> one month (condominium flat unchanged) 422545.26; foreclosure_referred without referral_date -> counted 0 days, initial charge, approval unchanged; extension_period with deadline 10 days out -> window 10, statement 422118.71; later accepted sell_property declaration -> credit 0.00, approval 424685.66; LESA balance 3000.00 -> disbursements limited in type order, statement 419824.86; returned cashier's check -> 35.00 fee, remittance 244243.21; a customer-wide (unscoped) reading of the extensions would count the 2021 extension and give approval 424435.66, which the case-scoped rule excludes.

STANDARD SOLUTION / WRITES. 1 record_payoff_daily_accrual_16b003bd per_diem_amount 85.31; 2 issue_retention_payoff_statement_a856e53a good-through 2026-10-29, balance 422545.26; 3 approve_appraisal_based_payoff_a02ac9a5 basis 640000.00, required 424310.66; 4 (user) remit_borrower_payoff_funds_17f1493b wire 'Lorraine Whitcombe' 244233.21. Verification: /tmp scratch harness replays the real tools and evaluates every compute on handling-time worlds; outputs equal computations and gold.

REWORK ROUND 3. R2-N1: the clearing cushion is per diem collected in advance; on satisfaction it is kept only for the per diem the case owes for days its funds were credited after the good-through date (base interest_through_basis date_funds_received), and any unused cushion is refunded with the held excess. Lorraine's wire is credited 2026-10-14, before the 2026-10-29 good-through date, so the 426.55 cushion she sends is refunded in full after satisfaction; only the wire receipt fee, returned remittance fee, title search fee and release recording charge are retained. The scored amount 244233.21 is unchanged. Tie rules now stated and computed: several received bills of one type due on the latest due_date are taken together (XSUM); several inspection results on the latest date count vacant first, then unable_to_determine; several accepted intent declarations on the latest date state retain_property only if all do; fee months count from the latest accrual_period. Persona now says she sent a couple of wires (records: 1500.00 and 25000.00). Probes: same-day occupied_by_others result beside the vacant one -> per diem 85.31 (vacant counts); second received tax bill (500.00) on the same due_date -> 85.41; same-day sell_property declaration beside the retain one -> credit 0.00, approval 424685.66; duplicate fee posting for 2026-09 -> statement 422545.26.
user_scenario:
You are Lorraine Whitcombe, 82, a retired school librarian. Since last autumn you have lived with your daughter in Bend, Oregon; your condominium in Spokane has stood empty since you moved out. A letter came saying the reverse mortgage on the condo has been sent to a foreclosure attorney, and you do not want to lose the place: you intend to keep it in the family. You are calling to pay the reverse mortgage off today, sending the money by wire from your own savings account in your own name, and you would like to be told the amount to wire. You speak politely but a little anxiously, and you like to have figures repeated slowly.

You give your full name, Lorraine Whitcombe, at the start. Only when the representative asks to verify you do you give your phone number, 4155550147, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 5268. You do not know your loan number or any case number by heart and say so if asked; you ask them to look it up.

If the representative explains that something has to be prepared, figured or approved on their side before you send the money, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is needed on their side today. If they ask whether you live in the condo, you say you moved to your daughter's in Bend last October and the condo is empty. If they ask about money already sent, you say your sister Dana sent some by wire, that her bank pulled one of her wires back, and that you also sent a couple of wires and a few cashier's checks yourself, but you do not remember the amounts and ask them to go by their records. If an amount they quote seems much larger than you expected, you say it is more than you thought and ask them to check it against their records once, then accept the figure they confirm.

When the representative gives you the amount and hands you the way to send the funds, you send it yourself as a wire, with the sender name exactly 'Lorraine Whitcombe' and exactly the amount they gave you. When they tell you the money has been received, you thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain R -> P -> A -> X with no parallel prerequisites; each policy reads the field the previous write sets (per_diem_amount, statement_balance, required_payoff_amount), so only the order X, A, P, R reproduces the gold values.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the approval leaves required_payoff_amount at the statement balance 422545.26; the remittance becomes 242467.81 instead of 244233.21.
Skipping the statement leaves statement_balance 0.00, so the approval computes 1765.40 instead of 424310.66.
Skipping the daily accrual leaves per_diem_amount 0.00, so the statement balance is 420156.58 instead of 422545.26.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay off today, keep the condominium and be told the amount to wire; it never mentions a daily accrual, a statement, an appraisal or an approval, and consents only generically ("go ahead and do whatever is needed on their side today") after the agent explains that something must be prepared.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: record_payoff_daily_accrual_16b003bd, issue_retention_payoff_statement_a856e53a, approve_appraisal_based_payoff_a02ac9a5 and remit_borrower_payoff_funds_17f1493b each call only ctx.update/ctx.create with the passed values; none reads per_diem_amount, statement_balance or required_payoff_amount to refuse, so each stays callable while its prerequisite is unresolved.
